title: Quantifying Spatial Transfer Uncertainty in Coastal Solar Resource Assessment for Offshore Floating Photovoltaic Projects
content: Whether a nearby station can serve as a proxy for offshore solar irradiation depends on the time scale of the assessment. This study compared daily irradiation records from Taichung and Wuqi, Taiwan, using 731 paired dates in 2020–2021. The analysis compared signed differences, absolute differences, and upper percentiles, and used a moving-block bootstrap to examine seasonal contrasts. On identical dates, the mean absolute daily difference was 0.725 kWh m⁻². Averaging signed differences within months before taking absolute values reduced the paired-day-weighted measure to 0.477 kWh m⁻², a 34.2% reduction. The summer–autumn ranking reversed between daily and monthly scales in the pooled record, but not within either year. The 90th percentile of absolute daily differences was 1.383 kWh m⁻² across the full paired record. Summer and autumn had similar median differences, but their gap widened from 0.028 kWh m⁻² at the median to 0.219 kWh m⁻² at the 95th percentile. Monthly agreement can therefore conceal large daily differences relevant to station selection. The findings characterize interstation agreement for preliminary offshore photovoltaic (OFPV) screening; they do not quantify irradiation error at the Changhua offshore site.
